topic.title: Milk goes up in steps you will not fight
topic.claim: Milk is the one price you never argue about, which is exactly why it can go up Rs 4 in one step.
topic.behaviour: We spend weeks comparing a phone or a sale price. The litre of milk that arrives every morning gets a shrug and a paid-up monthly bill.
topic.mechanism: A daily purchase with no substitute gets no shopping around, so a price rise meets almost no resistance. People complain, then they pay, because the tea has to be made.
topic.group: Working households that run a monthly budget
topic.moment: You scroll through three sites to save Rs 500 on earphones, then pay the new milk price without reading the bill.

turn.believed: We are careful spenders who hunt for the best price.
turn.actually: We are careful only where there is a choice. Where there is none, the price just moves.

topic.feeling: Quietly squeezed, with nobody to argue with
topic.villain: A pricing model that sets rises on the things you cannot skip
topic.because: Dairies cite higher costs for fodder, cattle feed, packaging and transport. A product bought every single day passes those costs on with the least resistance.

proof.fact: Amul and Mother Dairy raised liquid milk prices by Rs 2 to 4 per litre, and Mother Dairy's hike was Rs 4 in a single step. Delhi consumers said earlier revisions were about Re 1 at a time.
October retail inflation was 6.09%, up from 5.5% in September, and food inflation was 8.94%.

topic.payoff: Make a list of the five things you buy every week without comparing. That is where your budget actually leaks.
topic.send_to: The friend who tracks every Swiggy coupon but never looks at the grocery bill
real_details: Consumers complained that prices are revised every few months, which makes monthly budgeting difficult.
Onions were ₹53.81 a kilo on 12 November against ₹26.91 a year earlier.
topic.news_peg: Amul and Mother Dairy raised milk prices from Thursday 12 November 2026, and retail inflation data released on 12 November showed 6.09% for October.
topic.why_now: Milk, onions and sugar all moved in the same month, and the budget feels it before the headline does.

score.why: We hunt for a Rs 500 saving on earphones and never question the milk bill; the list of things you never compare is a good test.
